text:
Dana: Heads-up: after the canary rollout for model-prod-3 we saw a weird oscillation in KV residency. not high error rate but obvious p95 latency blips for short requests.
Sahil: Can you paste the memory/eviction graph? Could be TTL bucketing + bursty prefixes causing churn.
Dana: attaching tiny excerpt from the node that flagged it — repeated eviction events every ~30s, lots of keys with short reuse but same prefix fingerprint.
Irene: quick thought — our residency heuristic scores entries by (last_access * size_penalty) and we quantize TTL into 3 buckets. if prefix keys cluster near bucket boundaries we might evict too aggressively.
Maria: @Irene is there a repro we can run locally to trigger the same pattern?
Dana: yes, I constructed a little load script that alternates long-context and short prompts against the same session id. small script:
```bash
# repro load (very small)
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST $API/complete -d '{"session":"sess-A","prompt":"short prompt"}' &
  sleep 0.02
  if (( i % 10 == 0 )); then
    curl -s -X POST $API/complete -d '{"session":"sess-A","prompt":"<long 800 token input>"}'
  fi
done
```
Sahil: interesting. so short requests are evicting between the long ones because their prefix keys are treated independently. are we coalescing prefixes across tokenization variants?
Irene: we do normalize prefixes for common tokenization, but the sticky/session key currently includes a short rolling counter for shard affinity, which might be creating distinct cache key variants that don't coalesce.
perf-bot: Perf alert: kv_eviction_rate increased 320% on node redwood-runner-7 over 2m during canary.
Maria: can we try two quick experiments: 1) temporarily increase session_ttl_ms to 120000 for the canary, 2) disable rolling-affinity-bit so the cache key is stable across warmups. small risk but low blast if limited to canary.
Dana: I can flip the TTL and run the repro; will collect kv_key_hit_seq and kv_residency_score histograms.
Irene: also add a metric: cache_reuse_window_ms (how long a prefix is used across requests). if it's often < 2s we might need micro-buckets for prefix hits.
Sahil: note: kernel selection might be indirectly related. when long contexts hit, we switch to chunked attention kernel which increases memory pressure briefly causing eviction windows to align with these switches. worth noting in traces.
Dana: good call — I'll capture trace level=debug for kernel switches during the run. payload snippet from the log:
```
2026-02-11T14:12:03Z runner-7 INFO kv: evict key prefix=0x7a2d reusetime=184ms size=48 residency_score=0.21
2026-02-11T14:12:03Z runner-7 INFO kernel: selected=chunked-attn seq_len=800 mem_delta=+120MB
2026-02-11T14:12:33Z runner-7 INFO kv: evict key prefix=0x7a2d reusetime=38ms size=12 residency_score=0.09
```
Maria: that log pretty clearly shows eviction aligned to kernel mem spikes. two prio actions: prevent unnecessary prefix-key divergence, and smooth eviction during kernel-induced memory pressure.
Irene: for longer-term: change key derivation to include a stable prefix fingerprint plus a session-stable salt (no rolling bit), then use an adaptive eviction penalty function that considers recent reuse frequency (exponential decay window).
Sahil: agree. short-term: TTL bump + disable rolling affinity for canary. long-term: key redesign + residency_score tweak + kernel mem-smoothing (e.g., prefetch backpressure).
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/config/ttl-bump-230112 -> runner-7 (scope: canary nodes)
Dana: running repro now, will post kv_key_hit_seq and p99 after 10m. tagging @Sahil @Irene. :mag:
Maria: thanks — if this fixes it we can roll to the rest of the cluster with a simple config flip. :thumbsup:
